newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs approve fair deal for workers abroad.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve fair deal for workers abroad.

text.p: Service sector workers posted to another European Union country will soon be assured of a fair deal after Euro-MPs agreed to planned EU rules on minimum pay, holidays and social security benefits.

The European Parliament voted on Wednesday in favour of a draft directive which aims, on the one hand, to set decent working conditions for workers on temporary contracts abroad and, on the other, prevent them from undercutting wage levels in the host country.
Workers on contracts of less than a month, or involved in what EU governments deem to be "insignificant" amounts of work, will not be covered by the directive's provisions on minimum rates of pay.
Nor can member states which do not have a minimum wage be forced by the directive - COM(93)225 - to introduce one.
The proposal, which was approved by EU social affairs ministers on June 3 after five years of wrangling, has the support of all member states except Britain and Portugal.
It needed the approval of the parliament to become law.

German Socialist Helwin Peter, the author of a parliamentary report on the directive, told the EU assembly on Tuesday the new rules would do much to combat wage dumping and make it easier for workers to move around the EU.
